title: Chapter 152: A Unique Charm
html:
At seven that evening, after two wrong turns, Liu Dao and Chen Ge finally reached their destination.

“Come on. I’ll introduce you to the rest of the studio crew.” Liu Dao parked and headed into the nearby woods.

“We’re on the outskirts of Jiujiang, right?” Before leaving the car, Chen Ge checked his backpack. Potholes riddled the neglected road, and a low mound of stones blocked part of it as though placed there deliberately. Tall, dense trees lined both sides, probably planted decades ago.

Their canopy swallowed the moonlight. Within the woods, darkness closed around them, and Chen Ge switched on his flashlight as he followed Liu Dao. Ten minutes later, they were still weaving among the trees.

“Brother, are we lost?” Chen Ge looked around. There was no sign that another person had ever passed this way.

“Don’t worry.” Liu Dao made a call, then turned down a narrow path. “The terrain is confusing, with no landmarks. It’s easy to lose your bearings. Since you’ll be entering the hospital alone, mark the trees as you approach so you can find your way back.”

After several more minutes, they finally emerged from the woods. A large tent stood in the clearing ahead.

“This is the only open ground nearby, and it has the strongest signal.” When the people inside spotted Liu Dao, they came out to meet him.

“Brother Liu, where have you been? You know we’re short-handed. Are you trying to work Sister Lee and me to death?” grumbled a blunt young man of about twenty, whose close-cropped hair made his head resemble an upturned bowl.

“Why did we send him to collect someone when we know he has no sense of direction?” Sister Lee asked. Rough-skinned and powerfully built, she was more muscular than most men.

To dispel the awkwardness, Liu Dao pulled Chen Ge forward. “This is Chen Ge, the host who’ll be livestreaming alone inside the Third Sick Hall. We still have some time. Teach him to operate the equipment and go over the camera techniques.”

“This is Chen Ge?” Sister Lee pushed Liu Dao aside. She and the young man studied their new host, bafflement flashing across their faces when they saw his equipment. Isn’t he filming a supernatural livestream? Why did he bring a rooster?

Both plainly wanted to comment, but first-meeting politeness kept them silent.

“I’m Zhang Ping, and this is Sister Lee. We’ll handle the relay for your livestream.” The young man led Chen Ge into the equipment-packed tent. He demonstrated the controls, then had Chen Ge open the black suitcase and explained each item inside.

Outside, Sister Lee lowered her voice. “Old Liu, are you sure this kid can deliver? We gave up the slots of two hosts with a hundred thousand viewers each just to secure a level-two recommendation. The platform is afraid of angering Qin Guang and is deliberately making things difficult for us.”

Liu Dao lit a cigarette. The platform ranked recommendations on five levels, with level one the strongest and level five the weakest. Level two was the best placement they could obtain for a newcomer.

“He gets one level-two recommendation, while Qin Guang has three level-one slots and a featured ad on the front page. The loser is obvious.” Sister Lee’s doubts had only deepened after meeting Chen Ge. A famous host needed either extraordinary looks or overwhelming charisma, and he seemed to possess neither. He looked like an ordinary man living an ordinary life—restrained and composed rather than theatrical. If anything, he resembled a doctor more than an entertainer.

“You’ve only seen the surface. Talk to him, and you’ll discover a unique charm. He understands fear differently from most people.” Liu Dao remembered his first conversation with Chen Ge, during which the other man had controlled every turn while one thought screamed through his mind: This man is insane!

Only later had he realized that they simply did not think on the same level.

“I’m not dismissing him, but we’ve invested too much in this.” Sister Lee sighed. “Securing him a recommendation will also put us in Qin Guang’s sights. The platform is promoting Qin Guang as its featured host. Once his position is secure, every other host in our studio will suffer.”

Liu Dao motioned for her to lower her voice. “Have some faith in Chen Ge. Both of Qin Guang’s last two broadcasts were imitations. The man inside that tent is the genuine article.”

“But he has no script, props, or actors. Who will watch a livestream that dull?”

“I’m not arguing with you. Just do your job and make sure we have no technical failures tonight.” Composing himself, Liu Dao entered the tent, greeted Chen Ge, and opened a bookmarked page on his laptop. “Come look at this.”

Chen Ge expected a script. Instead, the screen displayed a news article.

“A scripted broadcast would feel fake and be easy to expose, so we’ll leave the narrative to you.” Liu Dao pointed to the article. “This may offer some inspiration. Three mysteries about the hospital attract the most discussion online. First, the director disappeared; no one has confirmed whether he is alive or dead. Second, strange noises echo through the buildings every midnight. Third, bloody words appear from nowhere after dark and vanish at dawn. Several people swear they’ve witnessed them. Build the broadcast around those three points, and it should have a strong effect.”

Chen Ge nodded. Reading the reports gave him a clearer picture of the hospital.

“Let’s eat first, then discuss the remaining details.” Sister Lee distributed boxed meals from an insulated cabinet. At 9:30 p.m., Liu Dao stepped outside to make a call. When he returned, he told Chen Ge it was time.

While Zhang Pin unpacked the equipment, Chen Ge made his final preparations. He opened his bag and, under the crew’s curious stares, tugged the jacket away from the white cat and put it on.

The jacket carried the kittens’ scent. Unless Chen Ge wore it, the white cat would never follow him into the hospital.

“Why is everyone staring?” He tucked Xiaoxiao into a jacket pocket and released the cat. “A rooster, a doll, and a white cat are perfectly normal equipment for a supernatural livestream, aren’t they?”
